problemText: What is the sum of the interior angles of a convex hexagon (6 sides)?
hints: Use the interior angle sum formula (n - 2) × 180° with n = 6.
(6 - 2) × 180° = 4 × 180° — do not drop the subtraction of 2.

problemText: A regular pentagon has 5 congruent sides and 5 congruent angles. What is the measure of ONE interior angle?
hints: First find the total: (5 - 2) × 180°. Then use the fact that the pentagon is regular.
Divide the interior sum of 540° by the 5 equal angles.

problemText: A regular polygon has 15 sides. Taking one exterior angle at each vertex, what is the measure of ONE exterior angle?
hints: The exterior angles of any convex polygon add up to 360°, no matter how many sides it has.
The polygon is regular, so all 15 exterior angles are equal: 360° / 15.

problemText: Five of the six interior angles of a convex hexagon measure 110°, 130°, 96°, 142°, and 118°. Find the measure of the sixth interior angle. Type your answer as a number of degrees.
hints: The hexagon is not described as regular, so find the SUM first: (6 - 2) × 180° = 720°.
Add the five known angles (110 + 130 + 96 + 142 + 118 = 596) and subtract that total from 720.

problemText: The interior angles of a convex polygon add up to 1440°. How many sides does the polygon have?
hints: Set the formula equal to the given sum: (n - 2) × 180° = 1440°.
Divide both sides by 180 to get n - 2 = 8, then add 2 — the answer is not simply 1440 / 180.

problemText: In a regular polygon, each interior angle measures exactly 5 times its own exterior angle. How many sides does the polygon have?
hints: At any vertex the interior angle and its exterior angle form a straight line, so they add to 180°.
If the exterior angle is e, then 5e + e = 180°, so e = 30°. Now use the fact that the exterior angles of a regular n-gon are each 360° / n.

problemText: Which statement is true of EVERY parallelogram?
hints: Three of these describe special parallelograms — a rhombus, a rectangle, or a square — not every parallelogram.
A diagonal splits any parallelogram into two congruent triangles, which forces the opposite sides to match.

problemText: MNPQ is a parallelogram with its vertices named in order, so MN ∥ QP and NP ∥ MQ. If ∠N = 133°, what is m∠P?
hints: ∠N and ∠P sit across the parallelogram from each other — are they opposite angles or consecutive angles?
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are congruent; it is the CONSECUTIVE angles that are supplementary.

problemText: Parallelogram RSTU has its vertices named in order. RS = 14 and ST = 9. What is the perimeter of RSTU?
hints: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent, so TU = RS and UR = ST.
Perimeter = 2(14) + 2(9).

problemText: In parallelogram ABCD (vertices in order), side AB = 14 and side BC = 10. The perpendicular distance between the parallel sides AB and DC is 8. What is the area of ABCD?
hints: Area of a parallelogram = base × height, where the height is the PERPENDICULAR distance between the two parallel bases.
The slanted side of length 10 is not the height; pair the base 14 with the perpendicular distance 8.

problemText: In parallelogram JKLM the diagonals JL and KM intersect at point P. If KP = 4x - 3 and PM = 2x + 9, find the length of the whole diagonal KM. Type your answer as a number.
hints: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so P is the midpoint of KM: KP = PM.
Solve 4x - 3 = 2x + 9 to get x = 6, so KP = 21. Remember KM is made of TWO of those halves.

problemText: In parallelogram ABCD (vertices in order, so ∠A and ∠B are consecutive angles sharing side AB), the measure of ∠A is 40° less than three times the measure of ∠B. What is m∠A?
hints: Consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary, so ∠A + ∠B = 180°.
Let ∠B = b. Then ∠A = 3b - 40, so (3b - 40) + b = 180 gives b = 55; now compute ∠A, not ∠B.

problemText: Which quadrilateral is defined as a parallelogram with four right angles?
hints: One of these is a parallelogram with four congruent SIDES instead of four right angles.
Two of the choices are not parallelograms at all.

problemText: In rectangle ABCD (vertices in order) the diagonals AC and BD intersect at point E. If AC = 24, what is BE?
hints: A rectangle's diagonals are congruent, so BD = AC = 24.
A rectangle is also a parallelogram, so its diagonals bisect each other: BE is half of BD.

problemText: WXYZ is a rhombus with its vertices named in order. If m∠W = 104°, what is m∠X?
hints: A rhombus is a parallelogram first, so it keeps every parallelogram angle property.
∠W and ∠X are consecutive angles sharing side WX, so they are supplementary.

problemText: A rhombus has diagonals of length 30 and 16 that bisect each other at right angles. Find the length of one side of the rhombus. Type your answer as a number.
hints: The two diagonals cut the rhombus into four congruent right triangles whose legs are HALF of each diagonal.
The legs are 15 and 8, and the side of the rhombus is the hypotenuse: 15² + 8² = 289.

problemText: In rhombus JKLM (vertices in order), JK = 5x - 8 and KL = 2x + 7. What is the perimeter of JKLM?
hints: All four sides of a rhombus are congruent, so 5x - 8 = 2x + 7.
Solving gives x = 5, so each side is 17. The question asks for the perimeter, not one side.

problemText: In rhombus ABCD the diagonals AC and BD intersect at point E. The perimeter of the rhombus is 60 and AE = 9. What is the length of diagonal BD?
hints: A perimeter of 60 with four congruent sides makes each side 15, and that side is the hypotenuse of right triangle AEB.
Legs: AE = 9 and BE = √(15² - 9²) = 12. BE is only HALF of BD.

problemText: The midsegment of a trapezoid connects the midpoints of which two sides?
hints: The bases are the parallel sides; the legs are the two non-parallel sides.
The midsegment runs parallel to the bases, so it cannot start or end on a base.

problemText: Trapezoid ABCD has its vertices named in order with AB ∥ DC, so AD and BC are the legs. If ∠A = 74°, what is m∠D?
hints: ∠A and ∠D are the two angles at the ends of leg AD, which acts as a transversal between the parallel bases.
Same-side angles along a leg are supplementary: 180° - 74°.

problemText: Kite PQRS has its vertices named in order, with PQ = PS and RQ = RS. If ∠Q = 88°, what is m∠S?
hints: The congruent side pairs meet at P and at R, so ∠P and ∠R are the vertex angles and ∠Q, ∠S are the non-vertex pair.
In a kite the congruent pair of opposite angles is the NON-vertex pair.

problemText: Kite ABCD has diagonals AC = 18 and BD = 11. Find the area of the kite. Type your answer as a number.
hints: The diagonals of a kite are perpendicular, which gives the area formula (d1 × d2)/2.
Multiply 18 × 11 = 198, then take half.

problemText: In trapezoid ABCD, AB ∥ DC with AB = 9 and DC = 21. Point M is the midpoint of leg AD and point N is the midpoint of leg BC. What is the length of MN?
hints: MN joins the midpoints of the two legs, so it is the midsegment.
The midsegment is the AVERAGE of the bases: (9 + 21)/2. Its length must land between 9 and 21.

problemText: Isosceles trapezoid ABCD has its vertices named in order with AB ∥ DC and congruent legs AD and BC. The angles at the two ends of leg AD are ∠A = (4x + 6)° and ∠D = (6x - 16)°. What is m∠A?
hints: ∠A and ∠D sit on the same leg between the parallel bases, so they are supplementary — not congruent.
Solve (4x + 6) + (6x - 16) = 180 to get x = 19, then substitute into 4x + 6 (not into 6x - 16).
